136	+### What is documented as retained but not resumable
137	+
138	+`workflow/CHEATSHEET.md` section 3 lists deadline, blocked worker, quota block, rejected completion file and blocked
139	+review. The mechanism is implicit: once `drive` has stopped the workers (`:812-816`), the next `wait_handoffs` takes

141	+resume reports `Invalid completion file for <lane>` rather than the original reason. For reviews, a `blocked` status

144	+`relaunched/<lane>/1/`) is commit `312a96d` on the unmerged branch `fix/worker-relaunch`; it is not in this tree, so a
145	+run whose workers were stopped has no continuation today.

147	+### Gaps and what I would change
148	+
149	+- The verifier and cherry-pick interruptions are the only places where a crash forces a manual command with no
150	+  integrity reason: the interrupted attempt has no evidence to protect. Recommendation 1 and 8 below.
151	+- Deadline-before-file ordering turns a controller outage into a lost run. Recommendation 2.
152	+- Accepted reviewer decisions should be durable at acceptance. Recommendation 4.
153	+- Print-transport reviews are not resumable and the docs say the opposite. At minimum the runbook and cheatsheet must
154	+  say it; Recommendation 6 removes the asymmetry.
155	+- Good practice (LangGraph interrupts with idempotent nodes) is followed for handoff, freeze, review and integrate,
156	+  each guarded by a durable marker; the verifier is the one node without a marker for "started but not finished".

158	+## 2. Failed checks
159	+
160	+**Answer.** Nothing ever goes back to a worker: workers are stopped before any check runs, every retry reruns the same
161	+immutable snapshot commit, and a failure at the cap or an identical repeat ends the run so the operator starts a new
162	+run with changed code. A lane whose own checks passed is not rerun when a sibling fails, but the run as a whole waits,
163	+and in the candidate phase every lane is checked again on the combined revision.
164	+
165	+### How it works
166	+
167	+`freeze` validates the handoffs, calls `stop_workers` and only then snapshots (`workflow/pipeline.py:372-381`). Each
168	+`verify_<lane>` node checks `snapshots[lane]["commit"]` (`:446-450`) in a fresh worktree at that commit
169	+(`workflow/checks.py:154-158`). The prompt sent to workers says the controller's checks decide acceptance
170	+(`workflow/automatic.py:72-74`), and no code path writes to a lane's worktree or session after freeze.
171	+
172	+**Worker-phase gate.** `evaluate_worker` gates every lane-local kind (`unit`, `contract`, `integration`) and verifies
173	+argv, worktree and timeout for every check (`workflow/verification.py:161-170,173-176`); `build` and `browser`
174	+checks are executed and recorded but their outcome is deferred (`DEFERRED_WORKER_KINDS`, `:25,151-153,159,171-172`),
175	+and `recheck_packet` keeps a deferred check's capture errors out of the gate (`workflow/checks.py:269-273`). The verify
176	+event says `recorded for the candidate gate: ...` (`workflow/pipeline.py:466-469`). Tested:
177	+`VerificationTests.test_worker_phase_records_build_and_browser_without_gating`,
178	+`..test_worker_phase_still_checks_deferred_command_integrity_and_lane_local_kinds`,
179	+`..test_recheck_packet_keeps_deferred_capture_errors_out_of_the_worker_gate`.
180	+
181	+**Combined-candidate gate.** `candidate` first rechecks every worker packet (`Worker evidence no longer passes`,
182	+`:476-480`), cherry-picks the selected lanes in declared order onto `base_commit` (`:488-492`), then runs every lane's
183	+checks on the combined revision with `phase="candidate"`, where nothing is deferred (`:495-505`,
184	+`workflow/verification.py:151-152`). The loop raises at the first failing lane (`:503-504`), so lanes later in
185	+declared order are not checked in that attempt. Tested: `VerificationTests.test_candidate_phase_gates_on_build_and_browser`;
186	+the end-to-end runs in `ThreeLaneRun`, `PipelineTests` and `SharedGraphTests` produce candidate packets per lane.
187	+
188	+**Attempt limit.** `attempt` and `retry_check` read and write `attempts.json`, capped by
189	+`policy.max_verification_attempts` (default 3; `:424-439`); `validate_policy` requires at least two attempts when a
190	+drill is configured (`workflow/verification.py:90-92`). Tested:
191	+`PipelineTests.test_configured_failure_drill_reopens_checkpoint_and_enforces_attempt_cap`.
192	+
193	+**Automatic retry and the identical-failure stop.** `advance_failed_checks` (`workflow/automatic.py:700-735`) retries
194	+only pending `verify_<lane>` or `candidate` tasks whose current packet is not `passed`; before bumping it compares the
195	+gate reasons of attempts N-1 and N with the attempt directory neutralised (`gate_reasons`, `:691-697`) and stops with
196	+`<phase>/<node> failed identically on attempts N-1 and N; not transient, inspect <packet>` (`:718-723`); it checks
197	+every target against the cap before changing any counter (`Verification retry limit exhausted; work and evidence
198	+retained`, `:730-732`). Tested: `CompletionTests.test_identical_failures_are_not_retried` (including a path-bearing
199	+reason), `..test_stale_error_on_a_completed_sibling_does_not_block_retry`,
200	+`RetryAnyLane.test_advance_failed_checks_knows_every_selected_lane`,
201	+`SharedGraphTests.test_recovery_in_actual_new_controller_processes` (drill retried in a new process, `adapter: [1, 2]`).
202	+Recorded: `parallel-reviewers-001` burned candidate attempts 1-3 with byte-identical reasons apart from the attempt
203	+path (events 23-28, `verification/candidate/ui/{1,2,3}/packet.json`); commit `3c7354c` added the neutralisation and
204	+the path-free "no Playwright report written" reason (`workflow/checks.py:246-249`).
205	+
206	+**Sibling lanes.** The verify fan-out runs in parallel (`workflow/pipeline.py:711-713,721`). When one lane fails,
207	+LangGraph keeps the successful sibling's write and only the failed task reruns; the sibling's packet digest is
208	+unchanged and no second attempt directory appears. Tested: `PipelineTests.test_failed_check_reuses_worker_and_successful_sibling`,
209	+`RetryAnyLane.test_retry_reruns_only_the_failed_lanes_check`. The passing lane is still affected in the sense that
210	+the run does not proceed to candidate until every lane passes, and its work is rechecked in the candidate phase.
211	+
212	+**What the operator does after a candidate failure.** Nothing for the first two attempts: the supervisor restarts and
213	+retries. After the identical-failure stop or the cap, the operator inspects the packet, and: for an environment
214	+fault at the same revision, `retry "$RUN" --phase candidate --node <lane>` then `automatic --live` (the manual `retry`
215	+does not apply the identical-failure comparison, `workflow/pipeline.py:957-969`); for a code fault, a new run.
216	+Recorded practice diverges from the runbook: in `worker-lanes-001` and `project-workflows-001` the operator moved the
217	+attempt directories aside (`verification-attempts-1-3-tmpdir-bug/`) and reset `attempts.json` by hand (events 22-25
218	+and 23-27 respectively show "Attempt 1" running again). Nothing in the controller detects that: `attempts.json` and
219	+the packet directories are plain files with no digest of their own. The cap is therefore a convention, not an
220	+integrity boundary.
221	+
222	+### Gaps and what I would change
223	+
224	+- Candidate checks stop at the first failing lane, so a later lane's failure is only discovered on the next attempt.
225	+  Running every lane and raising once would use one attempt for the whole picture; it changes no boundary.
226	+- The manual `retry` bypasses the identical-failure comparison; that is acceptable because it is an explicit operator
227	+  act, but the runbook should say so.
228	+- Bounded retries are in place; the automatic retry does not distinguish an environment failure (missing browser,
229	+  `npm ci` failure) from a code failure, so environment failures on immutable code cost a run.
230	+
231	+## 3. Worktree safety
232	+
233	+**Answer.** Worktrees are isolated from the source checkout by path and by the pinned revision, ownership is enforced
234	+from the captured Git tree rather than from any report, snapshots are content-addressed commits, and every packet and
235	+artifact is hashed and rechecked at review, approval and integration. None of this is a sandbox: every worktree shares
236	+the source repository's object database and every file is writable by the same Unix user, so a worker with Bash can
237	+alter any lane's tree, the source checkout or the run directory, and only some of that is detected.
238	+
239	+### How it works
240	+
241	+**Isolation.** `prepare` refuses a run directory inside the repository (`workflow/sessions.py:189-190`), creates it
242	+`0700` (`:191-192`), and adds one detached worktree per selected lane at the verified revision, checking `HEAD` and a
243	+clean status (`:202-205`). `ClaudeSessions.__init__` re-verifies worktree paths and start revision on every load
244	+(`:233-238`). Each lane's session runs with `cwd` at its worktree and a private `TMPDIR` (`:274-276`,
245	+`workflow/interactive.py:143-152`). Verification worktrees are fresh per phase, lane and attempt
246	+(`workflow/checks.py:154-158`) with private `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `npm_config_cache`, a short private `TMPDIR` that is
247	+removed afterwards, `HERDR_*` and `PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT*` stripped, `CI=1` (`:162-185`); checks run with
248	+`shell=False`, `stdin=DEVNULL`, a new session and process-group kill on exit or timeout (`:25-49`). The candidate is a
249	+detached worktree at `base_commit` with hooks disabled during cherry-pick (`workflow/pipeline.py:488-492`); the review
250	+worktree is detached at the candidate commit (`workflow/automatic.py:403`). Tested: `SessionTests.test_exact_revision_and_distinct_worktrees`,
251	+`..test_lock_and_dirty_worktree_fail_closed`, `PipelineTests.test_complete_offline_graph_with_real_browser_and_explicit_gates`
252	+(tmpdir length and removal), `InteractiveTests.test_reviewer_launch_requires_the_clean_candidate_worktree`.
253	+
254	+**Ownership against captured files.** `freeze` computes `changed_files` from `git diff --name-only` against
255	+`base_commit` plus untracked files not ignored (`workflow/pipeline.py:211-214,390`), refuses a moved `HEAD`
256	+(`Worker changed HEAD`, `:388-389`), checks each path with `safe_path` (no `..`, no absolute, no wildcards;
257	+`workflow/verification.py:38-42`) against the lane's prefixes with `owns` (`:45-46`) and against every excluded lane's
258	+prefixes (`Ownership violation: <lane> edited <path>, owned by excluded lane <other>`, `:383,393-397`), refuses
259	+symlinks (`:398-399`), stages into a private index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `:400-407`) and then requires the captured tree's
260	+diff to equal the list it checked (`Files changed during snapshot; refuse inconsistent evidence`, `:409-411`).
261	+`evaluate_worker` re-applies ownership to the packet's `changed_files` in the worker phase (`:128-131`). Tested:
262	+`PipelineTests.test_ownership_violation_blocks_snapshot`, `SubsetSelection.test_selected_lane_touching_an_excluded_lanes_path_blocks_at_freeze`,
263	+`VerificationTests.test_overlapping_ownership_and_unsafe_paths_are_rejected`, `..test_path_prefix_is_not_a_glob`.
264	+Untested: the symlink refusal and the changed-during-snapshot check.
265	+
266	+**Immutable snapshots.** The snapshot is `commit-tree` on the captured tree with a fixed author (`:412-415`), pinned
267	+under `refs/workflow/<sha256(run dir)[:16]>/<lane>` (`:416-417`) and recorded by SHA in `snapshots.json` with the
268	+lane's native session id (`:418-420`). The worker's own `HEAD` and index are untouched. Verification, candidate and
269	+review all address the SHA. A commit is immutable by construction; its reachability is not: the ref lives in the
270	+shared `.git` and nothing protects it from `git update-ref -d` or a later `gc` once the ref is gone. Untested beyond
271	+the end-to-end runs.
272	+
273	+**Evidence hashing and recheck.** `Capture.add` copies each artifact under a hash-bearing id, `0400`, and records its
274	+SHA-256 (`workflow/checks.py:82-97`). `evaluate_worker` resolves artifacts inside the registry root and recomputes
275	+hashes (`workflow/verification.py:132-143`), checks PNG headers (`:191-195`) and distinct screenshots (`:196-197`).
276	+The bundle records each packet's SHA-256 (`workflow/pipeline.py:509`); `validate_bundle` re-hashes every packet,
277	+requires it inside the run directory and re-evaluates its gate (`:524-536`), and is called at review entry
278	+(`:675`), by `validate_review` (`:538-541`), at approval (`:687,943`) and integration (`:544`). `review.diff` is hashed
279	+into the status file and rechecked, and the review worktree must still be clean at the candidate commit
280	+(`workflow/automatic.py:579-582,668-671`). Tested: `PipelineTests.test_failed_check_reuses_worker_and_successful_sibling`
281	+(tampered artifact refused), `VerificationTests.test_tampered_artifact_and_registry_escape_block`,
282	+`NativeReviewerTests.test_reviewer_worktree_change_is_refused`, `..test_evidence_change_during_review_is_refused`.
283	+
284	+**Worktrees after a run and stale registrations.** Nothing deletes worktrees (`workflow/RUNBOOK.md`, "Stopping an
285	+unfinished run"). Each is registered in the source repository's `.git/worktrees/`; at audit time the source checkout
286	+lists 33 registrations, none prunable, seven `refs/workflow/*` refs. `export` works when worktrees are gone
287	+(`ExportRuntime`, `workflow/pipeline.py:569-597`; `ExportRunTests.test_legacy_run_directory_re_exports_to_current_version_and_stays_stable`).
288	+A stale registration cannot collide with a new run because every path embeds the run id, phase, lane and attempt;
289	+`git worktree add` at a registered path fails, which is how `Partial candidate worktree exists` and `Interrupted
290	+check attempt exists` surface (`:485-487`, `workflow/checks.py:152-153`). There is no `prune` step and no test.
291	+
292	+**What a worker can do to another lane's tree or the source checkout.** In automatic mode a worker has
293	+`--tools Read,Glob,Grep,Edit,Write,Bash --permission-mode bypassPermissions --dangerously-skip-permissions`
294	+(`workflow/interactive.py:189-191,201-206`), no `--add-dir` restriction and the account's shell. It can write into
295	+another lane's worktree (detected only if the write lands outside that lane's owned paths, and then blamed on that
296	+lane at freeze), write into the source checkout (detected as `Source worktree is dirty` at integration,
297	+`workflow/pipeline.py:554-555`, and `No verified feature-branch completion` at the end of `drive`,
298	+`workflow/automatic.py:790-794`; not detected before), run any `git` command against the shared repository
299	+(reset the source branch: detected by `Source advanced since preparation` and `Source branch changed`, `:552-553,561-562`;
300	+delete refs or worktrees: not detected), and write anything in the run directory (see section 6). The
301	+`RUNBOOK.md` "Guarantees and boundaries" says plainly this is a trusted local tool, not a sandbox; that statement is
302	+accurate.
303	+
304	+### Gaps and what I would change
305	+
306	+- `refs/workflow/*` should be verified to still resolve to the recorded SHA at `validate_bundle` time, and the
307	+  candidate should be re-derivable from `snapshots.json` alone.
308	+- The symlink and changed-during-snapshot refusals need tests; they are the two ownership guards without one.
309	+- A `workflow prune` that removes only worktrees whose run directory no longer exists would keep the source
310	+  repository's registry bounded; it changes no evidence.
311	+- Least privilege is honoured for reviewers and verifiers, not for workers; that is a documented decision, and the
312	+  document should stop calling worktrees "isolation" for workers.

314	+## 4. Blocked and stuck sessions
315	+
316	+**Answer.** A session in native state `blocked` (question, permission prompt, refusal) is waited for until its own
317	+deadline, announced once on the timeline; a session missing from the inventory ends the run at once; a session that
318	+never writes its completion file ends the run at its deadline. The attention path is tested with a fake inventory and
319	+therefore proven without a live session, but only at the wait-loop level and only for the state word the code
320	+expects.
321	+
322	+### How it works
323	+
324	+`wait_handoffs` (`workflow/automatic.py:113-141`) per lane and per two-second poll: raise at the deadline
325	+(`Worker <lane> deadline exhausted; no automatic relaunch`, `:118-120`); raise if `locate` returns `None`
326	+(`Native worker missing; reconciliation required`, `:121-123`); on state `blocked` write one `interactive` event
327	+`Worker <lane> needs attention in its pane (native state blocked); waiting until its deadline` and keep polling
328	+(`:124-133`); accept a completion file only when the state is `idle` or `done` (`:134-136`). `read_completion` raises
329	+`Worker <lane> explicitly blocked: <summary>` for a file with `status: blocked` (`:92-93`). In `drive` every exception
330	+other than `KeyboardInterrupt` is recorded as `blocked`, the workers are stopped and the step exits non-zero
331	+(`:809-818`), which the supervisor turns into `Automatic controller blocked (exit 1)` (`:750-751`).
332	+
333	+`locate` (`workflow/interactive.py:64-105`) returns `None` when the receipt or the inventory row is absent, raises on a
334	+changed plan digest, an ambiguous or foreign row, a changed UUID, a state outside `idle|working|blocked|done`
335	+(`:96-97`) or a dead PID (`:98-104`). A raise inside the poll is treated like any other failure: the run stops. The
336	+recorded run `worker-lanes-001` event 6 shows an inventory error (`claude` not on `PATH`) ending the wait this way.
337	+
338	+`wait_reviews` mirrors this for reviewers with the reviewer's own deadline (`:351-354`), missing session
339	+(`:355-357`), `blocked` announcement (`:358-362`) and idle-only acceptance (`:363`); `_accept_native` then stops every
340	+reviewer on any failure (`:589-599`).
341	+
342	+Permission prompts cannot occur for workers (permissions are bypassed) and cannot block a reviewer (mode `dontAsk`
343	+denies silently); what the native harness reports as `blocked` for them is a question or a refusal. The controller
344	+does not read transcripts, so it cannot tell which.
345	+
346	+### What proves it
347	+
348	+- Attention path: `CompletionTests.test_blocked_worker_waits_for_attention_instead_of_ending_the_run` (fake inventory
349	+  rows: one event, sibling keeps running, deadline ends it, and a later `idle` accepts the file);
350	+  `ReviewCompletionTests.test_wait_accepts_only_idle_reviewers_with_files_and_never_relaunches` (same for
351	+  reviewers, including `working` and `done`). Both use `SimpleNamespace` sessions, so yes, provable offline. Neither
352	+  drives the graph: no test asserts that `drive` leaves the other lanes running after a `blocked` sighting; the
353	+  drive-level test `test_deadline_or_blocked_worker_stops_workers` injects the deadline error directly.
354	+- Never writes a file: `CompletionTests.test_idle_without_signal_times_out_not_completes`,
355	+  `..test_completion_while_working_is_not_accepted`,
356	+  `NativeReviewerTests.test_reviewer_deadline_without_a_file_stops_the_reviewers_and_launches_no_second`,
357	+  `ParallelReviewerScenarios.test_one_times_out`.
358	+- Explicit `blocked` file: `CompletionTests.test_foreign_and_blocked_signals_fail_closed`.
359	+- Missing from inventory: reviewers, in `test_wait_accepts_only_idle_reviewers_with_files_and_never_relaunches`
360	+  (`del self.rows[last]`) and `NativeReviewerTests.test_reviewer_missing_after_the_file_is_refused`; workers, untested
361	+  (`Native worker missing` appears in no test).
362	+- That the live `claude agents --json` reports the word `blocked` is assumed from `locate`'s allowed set; commit
363	+  `3c7354c` says it was seen live in `parallel-reviewers-001` (event 6 carries the pre-fix message).
364	+
365	+### Gaps and what I would change
366	+
367	+- `Native worker missing` tells the operator to reconcile, but `reconcile` only handles pending `launch_*` steps
368	+  (`workflow/pipeline.py:948-956`); during the handoff wait there is no reconciliation command, so this is a terminal
369	+  condition dressed as a recoverable one. A session that exited after writing a valid completion file should be
370	+  accepted, since the snapshot comes from the worktree, not the session (Recommendation 3).
371	+- Transient inventory failures (timeout, `claude` missing) end the run; they should be retried for a bounded number
372	+  of polls (Recommendation 7).
373	+- The `attention` event maps to viewer status `running` (`server/projects.ts:329-333`), so the viewer cannot show
374	+  that a lane is waiting for a human (Recommendation 9).

376	+## 5. Session identity and reconciliation
377	+
378	+**Answer.** A completion file is accepted only when its `launch_token` equals the token pinned in `plan.json` at
379	+prepare (workers) or generated per reviewer per review (reviewers), the run id and node id match, and the session the
380	+receipt binds is present in the native inventory and idle. The controller never learns which process wrote the file;
381	+the token is a shared secret readable by every same-user process, so identity is "the operator's environment attests
382	+it", as the runbook says.
383	+
384	+### How it works
385	+
386	+- **Launch tokens.** `prepare` stores a `uuid4` under `plan.nodes[<lane>].session_id` (`workflow/sessions.py:199-200`);
387	+  despite the key name it is the launch token, copied into the receipt as `launch_token`
388	+  (`workflow/interactive.py:180`) and into the worker's prompt (`workflow/automatic.py:63-74`). Reviewer tokens are
389	+  fresh `uuid4` per reviewer per review, stored in the status file and the prompt (`:510,519`).
390	+- **Receipts.** `run` writes the receipt before issuing `claude --bg` (`workflow/interactive.py:180-184`), so an
391	+  existing receipt is proof that a launch may have happened and forbids a second one (`:172-173`). `launch` runs the
392	+  helper once, then `settle` polls for the exact row (`:143-165,107-129`); on any failure the receipt is
393	+  `needs_reconciliation` (`:160-162`).
394	+- **Native UUIDs.** `locate` binds by `background_id` (from the receipt or, before it was bound, from the single
395	+  `claude attach <id>` line in the launch log; `:70-81`), then requires kind `background`, the node's worktree as
396	+  `cwd`, the expected name, an unchanged `sessionId`, a well-formed UUID, an attachable state and a live PID
397	+  (`:82-105`). The bundle's `snapshots[<lane>].session_id` is the native UUID from the receipt (`workflow/pipeline.py:418-419`).
398	+- **Completion binding.** Workers: `read_completion` (`workflow/automatic.py:77-94`). Reviewers:
399	+  `read_review_completion` validates the schema, then run id, node id, that reviewer's token, bundle digest and
400	+  candidate commit, then the finding vocabulary (`:295-317`).
401	+- **Independence.** `check_independence` requires each reviewer's located row to carry the recorded UUID, distinct
402	+  from every worker UUID in the bundle and from every other reviewer (`:557-566`); `check_reviewers` and
403	+  `check_review` re-apply the distinctness rules on the persisted record (`workflow/pipeline.py:108-131,145-147`).
404	+  Print reviewers get controller-generated UUIDs passed with `--session-id` and echoed back in the result
405	+  (`workflow/automatic.py:617,633,654`).
406	+- **reconcile.** CLI `reconcile` only accepts a run whose `state.next` still has `launch_*` steps with receipts and
407	+  calls `sessions.run`, which rebinds through `reconcile` and never launches (`workflow/pipeline.py:948-956`,
408	+  `workflow/interactive.py:131-141`). Reviewers are rebound by `rebind_reviewers` and `Pipeline.reconcile_reviewer`
409	+  (`workflow/automatic.py:413-439`, `workflow/pipeline.py:313-326`).
410	+- **Stops.** `stop_session` persists the intent (`background_id`, `session_id`, `pid`) before signalling, re-locates
411	+  and refuses a changed identity, then requires the UUID and PID to be gone (`workflow/pipeline.py:328-354`);
412	+  `stop_workers` additionally refuses a restarted UUID (`:356-362`).
413	+- **What a relaunched attempt archives.** Not in this tree. On branch `fix/worker-relaunch` (commit `312a96d`),
414	+  `relaunch_worker` moves `<lane>.interactive.json`, `<lane>.launch.log`, `<lane>.prompt.txt` and `<lane>.stop.json`
415	+  to `relaunched/<lane>/<attempt>/`, refuses a lane with a completion or handoff file, an unconfirmed stop or a
416	+  still-alive session, launches once and sets `attempt + 1` on the new receipt. The launch token is not rotated
417	+  (`plan.json` is unchanged), which the recorded `parallel-reviewers-001/relaunched/adapter/1/adapter.interactive.json`
418	+  confirms (same `launch_token` as the live receipt). `worker-lanes-001` event 11 ("Operator attests native session
419	+  ... is idle") matches no commit in the repository; it was appended out of band.
420	+
421	+### What proves it
422	+
423	+`InteractiveTests.test_native_launch_and_reconciliation_never_spawn_duplicate`, `..test_launch_waits_for_native_pid_to_register`,
424	+`..test_launch_gives_up_when_pid_never_registers_without_relaunch`, `..test_launch_identity_mismatch_fails_immediately`,
425	+`..test_ambiguous_launch_never_retries_when_session_missing`, `..test_launch_intent_can_reconcile_exact_surviving_session`,
426	+`..test_foreign_or_exited_sessions_cannot_be_attached`, `..test_locate_reviewer_binds_the_review_worktree`;
427	+`CompletionTests.test_foreign_and_blocked_signals_fail_closed`; `ReviewCompletionTests.test_stale_foreign_or_malformed_completions_fail_closed`
428	+(wrong bundle, token, candidate, run, node, other reviewer's token, version, extra key, verdict, lane, `both`, missing
429	+link, empty requirement, malformed JSON, symlink); `NativeReviewerTests.test_reviewer_identity_changed_after_the_file_is_refused`,
430	+`..test_reviewer_that_is_a_worker_session_is_not_independent`, `ParallelReviewerScenarios.test_shared_identity`,
431	+`..test_wrong_node`; `PipelineTests.test_native_reviewer_stop_rechecks_identity_and_records_intent`,
432	+`..test_failed_stop_and_lingering_pid_block_freeze`. Untested: the CLI `reconcile` action itself, and any relaunch
433	+(its tests live on the unmerged branch).
434	+
435	+### Gaps and what I would change
436	+
437	+- The worker token is stored in `plan.json` under a key named `session_id`, which every worker can read with its
438	+  file tools. Section 6 covers the consequence. Renaming the key would remove a standing source of confusion.
439	+- Print transport skips `check_independence`; the persisted record is still checked by `check_reviewers`, so the
440	+  gap is only that a print reviewer's row is never compared against a live inventory (there is none).
441	+
442	+## 6. Permissions and blast radius
443	+
444	+**Answer.** A worker can execute anything the account can and write anywhere the account can; a reviewer can read the
445	+candidate worktree and the run directory and write exactly one file; nothing technical stops a worker from
446	+committing, pushing, editing another lane's files or the run directory, only detection at freeze and integration, the
447	+prompt text, and the fact that the source branch is a `feature/` branch that nobody merges.
448	+
449	+### What each session gets
450	+
451	+| Session | Command line | Effective authority |
452	+| --- | --- | --- |
453	+| Worker, manual mode | `claude --bg --name workflow-<run>-<lane> --safe-mode --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config {} --tools Read,Glob,Grep,Edit,Write --permission-mode manual <prompt>` (`workflow/interactive.py:189-206`) | file tools with operator prompts, no shell, no MCP |
454	+| Worker, automatic mode | same plus `,Bash`, `--permission-mode bypassPermissions --dangerously-skip-permissions` (`:190-191,203-205`) | full shell as the account; prompt says do not commit, push, launch agents or leave the worktree (`:192-195`, `workflow/automatic.py:67-74`) |
455	+| Native reviewer | `claude --bg --name workflow-<run>-reviewer[-<id>] --safe-mode --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config {} --tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write --allowedTools Edit(//<run>/<node>.completion.json) --add-dir <run> --permission-mode dontAsk <prompt>` (`:238-245`) | read candidate worktree and run directory; one permitted write |
456	+| Print reviewer | `claude --print --output-format json --session-id <uuid> --safe-mode --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config {} --tools Read,Glob,Grep --permission-mode dontAsk --permission-prompts none --add-dir <run> --json-schema <schema>` (`workflow/automatic.py:633-636`) | read only; verdict through structured output |
457	+| Verifier | policy `setup` and `checks` argv, `shell=False`, isolated env, per-check timeout, process-group kill (`workflow/checks.py:25-49,218-259`) | whatever the committed policy commands do, as the account |
458	+
459	+`HERDR_*` is stripped from every launch environment so a session cannot drive the operator's terminal
460	+(`workflow/interactive.py:145`, `workflow/checks.py:162`, `workflow/sessions.py:274`). `preflight` only checks that the
461	+CLI advertises the flags (`workflow/pipeline.py:803-810`); what `--safe-mode` does is not verified by any code or test
462	+in this repository. Tested: `InteractiveTests.test_automatic_permission_bypass_is_run_scoped`,
463	+`..test_native_launch_and_reconciliation_never_spawn_duplicate`, `..test_reviewer_launch_is_read_only_except_its_completion_file`
464	+(the flags, their order, cwd and environment), `GraphFixture` fake reviewer (asserts print jobs get
465	+`Read,Glob,Grep` and no bypass). Untested: that `dontAsk` plus the `Edit(//path)` rule denies every other write; the
466	+comment at `workflow/interactive.py:234-237` says it was observed live, nothing asserts it.
467	+
468	+### What stops a worker
469	+
470	+- **Committing.** Nothing prevents it; freeze refuses a moved `HEAD` (`Worker changed HEAD`,
471	+  `workflow/pipeline.py:388-389`) and the run ends. A worker that commits and then resets `HEAD` back leaves no
472	+  trace the controller checks.
473	+- **Pushing.** Nothing. The source repository has an SSH `origin` with push access, every lane worktree shares its
474	+  configuration, and `git push` is one Bash call. The controller itself never pushes (no `push` anywhere in
475	+  `workflow/`; `SharedGraphTests.test_automatic_drill_review_and_feature_only_finish` asserts the test repository has
476	+  no remote, which says nothing about the real one).
477	+- **Editing another lane's files.** Nothing prevents it. Detected at that lane's freeze only if the path is outside
478	+  that lane's ownership; a write inside the sibling's owned paths is captured as the sibling's work and verified and
479	+  reviewed as such.
480	+- **Editing the run directory.** Nothing prevents it. Consequences by file: `plan.json` or `policy.json` changes are
481	+  caught by digest (`workflow/interactive.py:69-70`, `workflow/pipeline.py:257-258`); its own completion file is the
482	+  intended channel; a sibling's completion file can be forged because the sibling's token is readable in `plan.json`
483	+  and `read_completion` binds to the token only (`workflow/automatic.py:85-87`), which would freeze the sibling's
484	+  unfinished worktree once that sibling's session is idle; `events.jsonl`, `attempts.json` and, later, packets and
485	+  bundle are unprotected before the hashes that bind them exist, and a detached background process left by the
486	+  worker (Bash, `nohup`) survives `stop_session`, which checks the session's PID and UUID only
487	+  (`workflow/pipeline.py:340-352`), and could rewrite evidence after the hashes were computed if it also rewrites the
488	+  bundle and status files. All of this is the same-user trust the runbook declares.
489	+
490	+### Hostile repository content
491	+
492	+Task text is committed configuration and pinned into the plan (`workflow/pipeline.py:830-834`); READMEs, test
493	+fixtures and source files are read by the worker with no filtering. A prompt injection in any of them is executed by
494	+a worker with the account's shell; the limits are the ones above (detection at freeze and integration, review, no
495	+automatic merge to main, no push by the controller). For a reviewer, hostile content can at most change the verdict
496	+it writes, since it has no shell and one permitted write; the brief instructs it to treat repository content as data
497	+(`workflow/prompts/review.md`), and a wrong approval is caught by nothing else. A reviewer can read the other
498	+reviewers' completion files through `--add-dir` (the prompt tells it not to, `workflow/automatic.py:221-223`);
499	+independence between reviewers is by instruction. The verifier executes policy `setup` and `checks` from the
500	+candidate revision, so a worker can change what those commands do by editing files they read (a Playwright config, a
501	+test file under its owned paths); the argv is fixed, the code behind it is the candidate's.
502	+
503	+### Gaps and what I would change
504	+
505	+- Rotate or remove the shared-secret property of worker tokens: put each lane's token only in its own prompt file
506	+  (`0600`, already) and not in `plan.json`, or bind acceptance to the session transcript. Small change in
507	+  `workflow/sessions.py:prepare` and `workflow/automatic.py:read_completion`.
508	+- Record the `origin` URL at prepare and, at freeze, compare `git rev-parse origin/<branch>` before and after; a
509	+  pushed branch would then at least be detected.
510	+- State in the runbook that "worktree isolation" for automatic workers means path separation, not confinement.
511	+
512	+## 7. Parallel reviewers
513	+
514	+**Answer.** Every declared reviewer runs in parallel over one shared review worktree, each with its own token, receipt,
515	+completion file, status file, pane and deadline; the verdict is unanimous, the first accepted block, rejected file or
516	+expired deadline decides at once and the others are stopped and marked `superseded`. Print transport differs in
517	+collection order, in what a Ctrl-C does, in identity checks and in the absence of files, panes and human input.
518	+
519	+### How it works
520	+
521	+- **Declaration and briefs.** `plan.reviewers` from `feature.json` 2.1.0 (`workflow/launch.py:42-50`,
522	+  `workflow/pipeline.py:86-100`); absent means the single default reviewer `review` (`workflow/sessions.py:64-68`).
523	+  Each brief is followed by the same fixed blocks and a completion protocol naming that reviewer's node, token, file
524	+  and the other reviewers (`workflow/automatic.py:201-235`).
525	+- **Launch.** `_review_native` writes the combined status and one status per reviewer with fresh tokens, then
526	+  launches sequentially in declared order, saving after each (`:504-554`). Sessions share `review-worktree`
527	+  (`workflow/interactive.py:58-62`).
528	+- **Waiting and unanimity.** `wait_reviews` polls all receipts each round; a reviewer's file is accepted when its
529	+  session is idle and the file binds; `decision_blocks` (verdict not approved, or any unresolved P0/P1) returns
530	+  immediately (`:363-374`); otherwise it returns when every reviewer has an accepted decision (`:375-376`).
531	+- **Decision.** `combined_review` writes one entry per declared reviewer in order (`verdict` null when none), the
532	+  union of findings tagged with `reviewer`, `reviewer` as the comma-joined UUIDs, `verdict: blocked` if any reviewer
533	+  is undecided or blocks (`:459-473`); `_decide` persists `review.json` for any verdict, marks blockers `blocked`
534	+  and, on unanimity, every reviewer `succeeded` (`:476-493`). `supersede_running` marks reviewers still
535	+  `pending|launching|running` as `superseded` when the run is decided (`:288-292`); `_record_partial` keeps decisions
536	+  accepted before a deadline or rejection (`:496-501`).
537	+- **Per-reviewer deadlines.** Each counts from its own receipt's `launch_requested_at` (`:338-341,351`); the first
538	+  expiry raises, others' accepted verdicts are retained (`:352-354,595-596`).
539	+- **Stops.** After any decision every reviewer is stopped, failures collected (`:448-456,597-598,600-605`); an
540	+  unconfirmed stop after a successful decision is retried by a resumed controller (`:387-394,761-773`).
541	+- **Manual import per reviewer.** `review --reviewer <id> --review-file <file>` stores `<node>.imported.json` and
542	+  waits until every declared reviewer is imported, then `combine_imported_reviews` produces the same record shape
543	+  (`workflow/pipeline.py:906-935,178-188`); `approve` refuses until then (`:936-947`).
544	+- **Panes.** One pane per reviewer in declared order, best effort, a failure recorded but never fatal
545	+  (`workflow/pipeline.py:300-310`, `workflow/interactive.py:374-423`).
546	+
547	+### Where print transport differs
548	+
549	+`_review_print` (`workflow/automatic.py:609-688`) starts one `claude --print` job per reviewer in parallel, then
550	+waits on them **in declared order** (`:645`): a later reviewer's block is acted on only after every earlier job has
551	+finished or timed out; each job still keeps its own deadline measured from its own start (`:650`). There is no
552	+receipt, completion file, pane, human input or `stop.json`; processes are terminated with `terminate`
553	+(`:674-676,684-686`). Identity is the controller-chosen `--session-id` echoed in the result (`:654`), not an
554	+inventory row, so `check_independence` does not run. Any exception, including a Ctrl-C, terminates all jobs and marks
555	+the review `blocked`; the run is over (`:673-682`, section 1). The structured-output schema is generated from the
556	+run's lanes, so a finding naming a foreign lane fails validation before `check_finding_lanes` (`:159-172,657-658`).
557	+
558	+### What proves it
559	+
560	+`ParallelReviewerScenarios.test_two_approve`, `..test_one_blocks_while_the_other_is_still_working` (first reviewer
561	+`working`, second blocks: `superseded` and `blocked`, both stopped), `..test_p1_anywhere` (approval with an open P1
562	+recorded as blocked, raw decision kept), `..test_one_times_out` (A's verdict retained), `..test_wrong_node`,
563	+`..test_shared_identity`, `..test_interrupted_launch`; `SharedGraphTests.test_reviewer_block_preserves_branch_and_does_not_relaunch`
564	+(both transports, one and two reviewers); `NativeReviewerTests.test_unconfirmed_stop_after_acceptance_keeps_the_verdict_and_is_retried_on_resume`;
565	+`TwoReviewerCompletionTests` (every acceptance case with two reviewers); `PrintReviewerTests.test_print_mode_never_starts_a_native_reviewer`,
566	+`..test_print_findings_carry_worker_and_requirement_into_review_and_export`,
567	+`..test_print_finding_without_worker_is_rejected_by_the_schema_without_relaunch`;
568	+`DeclaredReviewers.test_manual_import_requires_every_declared_reviewer_before_approval`,
569	+`..test_manual_import_of_the_default_reviewer_keeps_the_single_file_flow`,
570	+`..test_automatic_run_with_declared_reviewers_launches_each_over_the_shared_worktree`;
571	+`InteractiveTests.test_declared_reviewers_get_one_pane_each_in_declared_order_right_of_the_workers`.
572	+Untested: the print collection-order consequence (a later block waiting on an earlier job) and Ctrl-C in print mode.
573	+Recorded: no run with two declared reviewers has completed yet; `workflow-audit-001` (this run) is the first.
574	+
575	+### Gaps and what I would change
576	+
577	+- Print jobs could be collected with `wait` on any process (poll loop) rather than in order; the runbook documents
578	+  the current order, so this is a small behavioural change with a test that blocks the second job first.
579	+- A blocked reviewer superseding the others discards their findings; the PRD chose this (section 7 of
580	+  `docs/PRD_PARALLEL_REVIEWERS.md`). Their transcripts remain, but nothing in `review.json` records what they had
581	+  found. Recording the other reviewers' files if they already exist at decision time would cost nothing.
582	+
583	+## 8. Evidence and the viewer
584	+
585	+**Answer.** `run-state.json` is a faithful projection of the checkpoint, the run's own files and the event log at the
586	+moment it was written, hashed where it points to packets; it is not a live view, it can be edited by any same-user
587	+process, and it lags mid-node progress, which the viewer fills from `events.jsonl`.
588	+
589	+### How it works
590	+
591	+- **What is written and when.** `export_state` (`workflow/export_state.py:218-244`) writes `version` 1.4.0,
592	+  `definition` (kept verbatim if the stored one names the same nodes, `:57-64`), `values` (the LangGraph state
593	+  values), `next`, `tasks` (name, error string, interrupt payloads, pending `result`), the copied `events`,
594	+  `verification_packets` with SHA-256, and the derived `review` and `inputs` sections; `updated_at` only changes when
595	+  the content changed (`:240-243`). `prepare` writes the first one (`workflow/pipeline.py:854`), `report` writes it at
596	+  every CLI boundary and every `drive` step (`:724-728`, `workflow/automatic.py:807,817,836`), `status` calls `report`
